name: Patronus
banner: Daily builds for testing. Not for production.
tagline: Patronus is a free, Gentoo-based firewall and router with an SD-WAN dashboard, written in Rust. Pre-1.0.
lead: A Gentoo-based firewall and router written in Rust and enforced by the kernel's nftables: a full appliance on x86_64 and aarch64, the same web UI on small home routers, and an SD-WAN dashboard.
what_html:
Patronus is a firewall and router aimed at the space pfSense and OPNsense occupy. From a web UI, an API and GitOps it configures nftables rules, aliases, GeoIP and threat feeds; interfaces with VLANs, bonds, bridges and PPPoE; multi-WAN failover and policy routing; WireGuard and IPsec (site-to-site and road warriors); DHCP, DNS and NTP; device segmentation, per-device DNS policy and a guest network; high availability with state sync; Suricata IDS/IPS; BGP/OSPF; and traffic insight. It ships as an ebuild whose USE flags choose what is compiled in, and every image comes in an OpenRC and a systemd variant.

It runs in tiers from one code base. The standard tier is a Gentoo system installed from the ISO. The embedded tier puts a Gentoo-built musl userland with the same web UI on routers OpenWrt supports, keeping OpenWrt's kernel and drivers: so far the GL.iNet GL-AR750S (MIPS) and GL-AX1800 (aarch64), tested on real units, with signed upgrades and a bootloader rollback.

It is a one-person project in early development. Every claim in its README is tied to a test in CI (the claims ledger), and the pfSense / OPNsense parity audit lists what is still missing.
status: Patronus is at version {version}, published as daily builds of the main branch. Configuration and on-disk formats can still change between builds. Do not put it in front of a network you cannot afford to lose.
works: Daily ISOs for x86_64 and aarch64, OpenRC and systemd: QEMU tests install each one with the graphical installer, the text wizard and an answer file (UEFI and BIOS on x86_64), reboot from disk and log in to the web UI. Only images that pass are published, each signed and with an SBOM.
The installer can put WAN, LAN and a management network on bonds and VLAN tags (DHCP, static or PPPoE WAN); a test cuts one bond member and the web UI stays reachable on the management VLAN.

Live traffic tests in network namespaces for each feature in the README (firewall and NAT, multi-WAN failover, VPNs, DHCP and DNS, segmentation, guest network, HA, IDS); CI fails if a README claim loses its test.
Crash and reboot safety: 30 power-cut rounds without losing or corrupting a saved rule, and a regression test that the firewall comes back after a failed first start at boot.
Embedded router images for the GL-AR750S and GL-AX1800, OpenRC and systemd: built, checked against the flash size, booted in a QEMU gate with the web UI, and upgraded with a bootloader rollback.
Wi-Fi features (per-device passphrases, automatic channel, band steering, Wi-Fi uplink) proven with real 802.11 associations on simulated radios.

Network map: every device on every LAN segment with live up/down (DHCP leases, the kernel neighbour table, an ICMP check, opt-in nmap and LLDP), export as PNG, SVG or Mermaid, read-only share links and a dashboard stats feed. The segmentation advisor flags a flat LAN and isolates IoT devices, cameras, printers and TVs in one step; proven with real packets in network namespaces and driven in Firefox.
gaps: No stable release yet (0.x versions only), and no release-to-release upgrade and rollback test of an installed appliance.

In progress, not merged: a security suite (managed IDS rule sets, DNS filtering catalog, brute-force bans, a LAN scan, CVE exposure of the router's own packages), captive portal, reverse proxy with ACME certificates.
aarch64 ISOs are tested under QEMU emulation; Wi-Fi is proven on simulated radios, and real radios depend on their drivers.
The automated security audit in the repo is not an independent review.
